wavelengths of the optical module and services are affected.

TEMP_OVER.name: TEMP_OVER
possible_causes: The set rotating speed of the fan board is excessively low.
The fan board is faulty.
The air filter is excessively dusty.
The ambient temperature is excessively high or excessively low due to a cooler or heater equipment fault.
The fan is not in position.
The board that reports the alarm is faulty.
TEMP_OVER.impact:
The excessively high or low temperature puts the system in a highly dangerous state. If the
system runs in this state for a long period of time, bit errors may be generated and services
may be interrupted. Therefore, the TEMP_OVER alarm must be handled in a timely manner.

TEST_STATUS.name: TEST_STATUS
TEST_STATUS.description: The board is in the test status
TEST_STATUS.impact: When this alarm occurs, a test command may affect the system.

TF.name: TF
possible_causes: The laser module is damaged, or the laser is aging.
The detection circuit of the board is faulty.
TF.impact: If a laser transmission failure occurs, services are interrupted.

THUNDERALM.name: THUNDERALM
THUNDERALM.impact:
The surge protection performance of the system deteriorates. If the equipment is attacked by a
strong current (for example, a strong lightning stroke), the boards in the subrack may fail. As
a result, the services are interrupted.

TIME_LOCK_FAIL.name: TIME_LOCK_FAIL
TIME_LOCK_FAIL.impact:
When this alarm is generated, the NE time is unlocked. As a result, the time of the slave NE
cannot trace the time of the master NE, and services are prone to bit errors. Therefore, handle
this alarm immediately after it is reported.

TIME_LOS.name: TIME_LOS
TIME_LOS.description: The loss of the timing source level
possible_causes: There are fiber failures or misconnections.
The service board is faulty.
The clock board is faulty.
TIME_LOS.impact:
When the alarm is reported, the time between the upstream and downstream NEs cannot be
synchronous, which may affect the quality of the service.

TIME_NO_TRACE_MODE.name: TIME_NO_TRACE_MODE
TIME_NO_TRACE_MODE.description: The time enters the non- trace mode
possible_causes: The priority table is not configured.

There are fiber failures or misconnections. OptiX OSN 8800/6800/3800 Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms Issue 01 (2017-03-31) Huawei Proprietary and Confidential Copyright © Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 1017
The attributes of the packets at the upstream NE are configured incorrectly.
The clock board is faulty.
TIME_NO_TRACE_MODE.impact:
When the alarm is reported, the time between the upstream and downstream NEs cannot be
synchronous, which may degrade the clock synchronization performance of the system. (For
the OCS system, that may affect the quality of the service.)

TR_LOC.name: TR_LOC
TR_LOC.description: The clock of the cross- connect board is faulty
TR_LOC.impact:
When this alarm occurs, the board cannot function properly. Services will not be affected if
the standby cross-connect board is faulty. However, services will be transiently interrupted
during the active/standby switchover if the active cross-connect board is faulty.

TS_CFG_MISMATCH.name: TS_CFG_MISMATCH
possible_causes: The configured timeslot of the board that reports this alarm is inconsistent with the received timeslot.
TS_CFG_MISMATCH.impact: If timeslot mismatch occurs, services cannot be received properly.

TU_AIS_VC3.name: TU_AIS_VC3
TU_AIS_VC3.description: A TU alarm indication signal in the VC-3 lower order path
TU_AIS_VC3.impact: When this alarm occurs, VC-3 path services are interrupted.

TU_LOP_VC3.name: TU_LOP_VC3
TU_LOP_VC3.description: An alarm indicating the loss of pointer in the VC-3 lower order path
TU_LOP_VC3.impact: When this alarm occurs, VC-3 path services are interrupted.

TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADE.name: TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADE
TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADE.description: D Downgrade of APS tunnel protection group

VCAT_LOA.name: VCAT_LOA
VCAT_LOA.description: Delay of multiframes exceeds the threshold
VCAT_LOA.impact:
When this alarm occurs, aligning the virtual concatenation delay times out during service data
transmission. As a result, the timeslots cannot form a data frame, and packet loss occur in the
services.

VCAT_LOM_VC3.name: VCAT_LOM_VC3
VCAT_LOM_VC3.description: The loss of the virtual concatenation multiframe in the VC-3 path
VCAT_LOM_VC3.impact:
l When this alarm occurs during data transmission, services will be transiently interrupted
during an automatic switchover performed by the link capacity adjustment scheme
(LCAS).
l If the LCAS is disabled, the services are interrupted.

VCAT_LOM_VC4.name: VCAT_LOM_VC4
VCAT_LOM_VC4.description: The loss of the virtual concatenation multiframe in the VC-4 path
VCAT_LOM_VC4.impact:
l When this alarm occurs during data transmission, services will be transiently interrupted
during an automatic switchover performed by the link capacity adjustment scheme
(LCAS).
l If the LCAS is disabled, the services are interrupted.

VLAN_SNCP_PS.name: VLAN_SNCP_PS
VLAN_SNCP_PS.impact:
l When switching is performed on the VLAN SNCP group, services will be transiently
interrupted.
l When the alarm is reported, the working channel or the protection channel of the VLAN
SNCP group may have faulty services that need to be restored.

VOADATA_MIS.name: VOADATA_MIS
possible_causes: Replacing an attenuation board or optical module makes the stored attenuation value issued by the NE software fall beyond the adjustable attenuation range of the new board.
VOADATA_MIS.impact: The service quality may be affected.

W_R_FAIL.name: W_R_FAIL
W_R_FAIL.description: Writing or reading chip register failed
W_R_FAIL.impact:
The board cannot work properly. In this case, the services may not be received or transmitted
properly. In addition, the board may fail to query the current performance value.

WA.name: WA
WA.description: VELEN_REPEATED Repeated wavelengths found during wavelength locking configuration

WRG_BD_TYPE.name: WRG_BD_TYPE
WRG_BD_TYPE.description: Real board is mismatched with configured board
possible_causes: The type of the logical board configured on the U2000 is different from the type of the physical board installed in the slot.
The board that reports this alarm is faulty.
WRG_BD_TYPE.impact:
If the type of the logical board is different from the type of the physical board, the board
cannot work properly, affecting services.

XC_UNSWITCH.name: XC_UNSWITCH
XC_UNSWITCH.description: The cross-connect matrix of the board is not switched
XC_UNSWITCH.impact: The services related to the board that reports the alarm are interrupted.

LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH.name: LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH
LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH.description:
This alarm indicates a mismatch of the optical module type and the fiber type. This alarm is
generated when the type of the optical module inserted into an optical port mismatches the
type of optical port.
possible_causes: The optical port type supported by the physical board does not match the type of the optical module inserted into the optical port. OptiX OSN 8800/6800/3800 Alarms and Performance Events Reference 3 Clearing Common Alarms Issue 01 (2017-03-31) Huawei Proprietary and Confidential Copyright © Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 395
LASER_MODULE_MISMATCH.impact: Services cannot be properly received or transmitted and even will be interrupted.

BWUTILIZATION_OVER.name: BWUTILIZATION_OVER
BWUTILIZATION_OVER.description:
The BWUTILIZATION_OVER is an alarm indicating that bandwidth usage exceeds the
threshold. If traffic received or transmitted by monitored objects such as traffic classification
exceeds the traffic threshold and the bandwidth usage exceeds the acceptable value, the
BWUTILIZATION_OVER alarm is reported.
possible_causes: The traffic received or transmitted by a monitored object exceeds the traffic threshold.
The configured bandwidth usage threshold for a monitored object is low.
BWUTILIZATION_OVER.impact: The alarm will cause network congestion.

CFG_DATASAVE_FAIL.name: CFG_DATASAVE_FAIL
CFG_DATASAVE_FAIL.description:
Failure to save configuration data. This alarm is reported when configuration fails to be saved
in the database.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
567
CFG_DATASAVE_FAIL.impact: Configuration data will be lost or the database will be damaged.

CLIENT_PROT_NOTSTART.name: CLIENT_PROT_NOTSTART
CLIENT_PROT_NOTSTART.description:
Client 1+1 protection group not started. This alarm is generated when a client 1+1 protection
group is not started because the configurations on the both sides of the working and protection
channels of the protection group do not meet the requirements of enabling the protection
group.
CLIENT_PROT_NOTSTART.impact:
The client 1+1 protection group does not perform switching in case of a service fault and
therefore the protection fails.

ELAN_SMAC_FLAPPING.name: ELAN_SMAC_FLAPPING
ELAN_SMAC_FLAPPING.description:
The ELAN_SMAC_FLAPPING alarm indicates that the source MAC address learned by an
E-LAN service undergoes a transfer. This alarm is reported when two ports on a bridge or VSI
learn the same source MAC address.

ETH_APS_PATH_MISMATCH.name: ETH_APS_PATH_MISMATCH
ETH_APS_PATH_MISMATCH.description:
The ETH_APS_PATH_MISMATCH alarm indicates that the working and protection paths of
the APS protection group differ between the two ends. This alarm is generated when the

working and protection paths at one end are different from the working and protection paths at
the other end.
possible_causes: The configured working and protection paths at the two ends differ.
The physical link is connected incorrectly.
ETH_APS_PATH_MISMATCH.impact:
Service protection fails.

ETH_APS_SWITCH_FAIL.description:
The ETH_APS_SWITCH_FAIL alarm indicates a protection switching failure. This alarm is
generated when the request signals in the transmitted automatic protection switching (APS)
frame are different from the bridge signals in the received APS frame and this symptom lasts
for 50 ms.
possible_causes: The configurations of the APS protection group at two ends differ.
The physical link deteriorates or is connected incorrectly.
ETH_APS_SWITCH_FAIL.impact:
Service protection fails.
The following figure shows the major suppression relationship between the alarm and other
alarms related to the ETH APS protection group.

ETH_APS_TYPE_MISMATCH.description:
The ETH_APS_TYPE_MISMATCH alarm indicates protection scheme mismatch. This alarm
is generated when the information in the received automatic protection switching (APS) frame
is different from the APS protection scheme specified at the local end.
possible_causes: The switching types are different.
The switching directions are different.
The revertive modes are different.
ETH_APS_TYPE_MISMATCH.impact:
This alarm may cause the APS protection failure, and therefore the service protection fails.

ETH_CFM_MACSTATUS.name: ETH_CFM_MACSTATUS
ETH_CFM_MACSTATUS.description:
The ETH_CFM_MACSTATUS is a remote MAC defect indication. This alarm indicates that
a continuity check packet carrying a port tlv or an interface tlv is received from a given
remote MEP.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
608
possible_causes: The residential port of the remote MEP encounters a MAC failure.
ETH_CFM_MACSTATUS.impact: The residential port of the remote MEP encounters a MAC failure.

ETH_SERVICE_CONFIG_FAIL.name: ETH_SERVICE_CONFIG_FAIL
possible_causes: The Ethernet service fails to be configured due to resource conflict. OptiX OSN 8800/6800/3800 Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms Issue 01 (2017-03-31) Huawei Proprietary and Confidential Copyright © Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 627
ETH_SERVICE_CONFIG_FAIL.impact:
The Ethernet service for which the alarm is reported fails to be created and other services are
not affected.

ETHOAM_DISCOVER_FAIL.name: ETHOAM_DISCOVER_FAIL
ETHOAM_DISCOVER_FAIL.description:
The ETHOAM_DISCOVER_FAIL is an alarm indicating the point-to-point Ethernet OAM
discovery failure. When the OAM protocol is enabled at the port of a board and the
negotiation with the opposite equipment fails, this alarm is generated.
ETHOAM_DISCOVER_FAIL.impact:
The ETHOAM_DISCOVER_FAIL alarm is generated when the system runs the IEEE
802.3ah OAM protocol. IEEE 802.3ah OAM is a link management protocol and is irrelevant
to services.

ETHOAM_RMT_CRIT_FAULT.name: ETHOAM_RMT_CRIT_FAULT
ETHOAM_RMT_CRIT_FAULT.description:
The ETHOAM_RMT_CRIT_FAULT is an alarm indicating that a critical fault occurs on the
remote end of point-to-point Ethernet OAM. When the port with the OAM protocol enabled
receives the OAM message that contains critical fault information from the opposite end, this
alarm is generated.
ETHOAM_RMT_CRIT_FAULT.impact:
The ETHOAM_RMT_CRIT_FAULT alarm is generated when the system runs the IEEE
802.3ah OAM protocol. IEEE 802.3ah OAM is a link management protocol and is irrelevant
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
630
to services. This alarm indicates that the signal loss alarm is generated at the receive end of
the opposite port.

ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP.name: ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP
ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP.description:
The ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP is an alarm indicating the loopback of the VCTRUNK
port that receives the OAM protocol packets in a point-to-point manner. If the VCTRUNK
port of a board receives the OAM protocol packets sent by itself or the board after detection
of the loop is enabled, the ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP alarm is reported.
ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP.impact:
In the case of the ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP alarm, the link of the VCG port is
configured with a self-loop. The U2000 provides a function of automatically shutting down
the port in the case of the ETHOAM_VCG_SELF_LOOP alarm. If the user enables this
function in advance, services of this port are interrupted. If the user does not enable this
function, a broadcast storm may occur.

EX_ETHOAM_MPID_CNFLCT.name: EX_ETHOAM_MPID_CNFLCT
EX_ETHOAM_MPID_CNFLCT.description:
The EX_ETHOAM_MPID_CNFLCT is an alarm indicating the maintenance point (MP) ID
conflict. This alarm is reported when an MP receives the message sent by another MP with
the same MP ID in a maintenance domain.
EX_ETHOAM_MPID_CNFLCT.impact:
The MP should be unique network-wide. The MP conflict can affect the protocol and cause
the LB and LT tests to become abnormal. The services may be incorrectly received.

EXT_MODULE_OFFLINE.name: EXT_MODULE_OFFLINE
EXT_MODULE_OFFLINE.description:
Extended wavelength module offline. This alarm is generated when a user has configured
services on the channel corresponding to an extended module, but the physical extended
module is offline.
EXT_MODULE_OFFLINE.impact: All services on the channel corresponding to the extended module are unavailable.

FEATURE_WITHOUT_LICENSE.name: FEATURE_WITHOUT_LICENSE
FEATURE_WITHOUT_LICENSE.description:
Service without license. This alarm is generated when a license-controlled feature is used but
the license for the feature is not installed.
FEATURE_WITHOUT_LICENSE.impact:
A user cannot create, enable, or modify the license-controlled service or feature, but can
query, delete, or deactivate the service or feature. The available services are not affected and
are still available, but the alarm is reported.

HSC_UNAVAIL.name: HSC_UNAVAIL
HSC_UNAVAIL.description:
Working/protection switching failure. This alarm is generated when the configured active and
standby boards fail to perform switching.
HSC_UNAVAIL.impact: The active/standby switching and backup functions are not available.

INNER_COMMUN_MISCON.name: INNER_COMMUN_MISCON
INNER_COMMUN_MISCON.description:
Incorrect connection between an internal network and an external network. This alarm is
generated when an internal network and an external network are incorrectly connected
because the ports on the equipment are incorrectly cascaded.
INNER_COMMUN_MISCON.impact:
The data about communication between the NE and boards becomes abnormal. As a result,
the configuration and query commands cannot be properly processed.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
681

LASER_HAZARD_WARNING.name: LASER_HAZARD_WARNING
LASER_HAZARD_WARNING.description:
Hazard related to laser levels. When a high-power laser is used in the optical transmission
system, the system may cause personal injuries. In this case, if the IPA function is disabled or
not configured, this alarm is reported prompting the user to configure the IPA function.
LASER_HAZARD_WARNING.impact: This alarm does not affect services; however, it might cause personal injuries.

LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT.name: LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT
LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT.description:
The LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT is an alarm indicating that the link-state pass through (LPT)
disables a service port. On the packet domain, upon detecting that a remote access-side port
fails or the LPT service network fails, the LPT disables the local access-side port and reports
this alarm.
possible_causes: A fault such as a port failure is detected on the remote access side. Figure 4-4 Detection of the LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT alarm - 1 LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT NE2 (local) Service network NE1 (remote) Access link 1 becomes faulty. Access link 2 User side - A User side -B Access-side port Network-side port

The LPT service network is faulty. Figure 4-5 Detection of the LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT alarm - 2 LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT NE2 (local) NE1 (remote) Access link 1 Access link 2 User side - A User side - B Access-side port Network-side port Service network LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT
LPT_CFG_CLOSEPORT.impact:
When this alarm is reported, a port is closed and services carried on the port are interrupted.
The services, however, are switched onto the backup link because the LPT function is
enabled.

LSR_INVALID.name: LSR_INVALID
LSR_INVALID.description:
The LSR_INV ALID is an alarm indicating an invalid optical module. This alarm is generated
when the optical module cannot pass authentication.
LSR_INVALID.impact: The optical port of the board cannot receive or transmit services. Services are interrupted.

MAINBD_SUBBD_MISMATCH.name: MAINBD_SUBBD_MISMATCH
MAINBD_SUBBD_MISMATCH.description:
In one PID group, the service processing board must match the service outputting board;
otherwise, the MAINBD_SUBBD_MISMATCH alarm is generated.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
736
MAINBD_SUBBD_MISMATCH.impact:
In a PID group, if the service outputting board does not support the service processing board,
the wavelength services on the service outputting board will not be affected, but the service
processing board will be unavailable.
For example, in a PID group where the NPO2 board and ENQ2 board are used together, if the
NPO2 board does not support the ENQ2 board installed in the corresponding slot, the
wavelength services on the NPO2 board will not be affected, but the wavelength services on
the ENQ2 board will be unavailable.

MCLAG_CFG_MISMATCH.name: MCLAG_CFG_MISMATCH
MCLAG_CFG_MISMATCH.description:
MC-LAG configuration mismatch alarm. This alarm is generated when the system detects that
the configurations at both ends of an MC-LAG are inconsistent.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
737
MCLAG_CFG_MISMATCH.impact: Negotiation of MC-LAG configuration fails and the services may be interrupted.

MODULE_COOLCUR_OVER.name: MODULE_COOLCUR_OVER
MODULE_COOLCUR_OVER.description:
Module cooling current exceeding the threshold. The alarm is generated when the cooling
current of the module is higher than the upper threshold or lower than the lower threshold.
MODULE_COOLCUR_OVER.impact:
The working performance and reliability of the module are affected. In general, service
quality is not affected; however, it will be affected if the alarm exists for a long time.
Therefore, the alarm needs to be handled in a timely manner.

MODULE_RATE_MISMATCH.name: MODULE_RATE_MISMATCH
MODULE_RATE_MISMATCH.description:
Signal rate mismatching an optical module. This alarm is generated when the optical module
does not support a mode, such as the speedup mode, specified by the user.
MODULE_RATE_MISMATCH.impact:
When this alarm occurs, services are unavailable or may be interrupted.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
744

MODULEFILE_UPDATE_FAIL.name: MODULEFILE_UPDATE_FAIL
MODULEFILE_UPDATE_FAIL.description:
Failure to update the microprogram and laser parameter table. This alarm is generated when
the in-service upgrade of the optical module microprogram and the parameter table on the
U2000 fails.
MODULEFILE_UPDATE_FAIL.impact:
l The upgrade of the optical module microprogram fails. As a result, the new
microprogram of the optical module is unavailable and the old one is still used.
l The upgrade of the laser parameter table fails.

MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL.name: MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL
MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL.description:
The MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL is an alarm indicating a failure to negotiate the OAM
protocol. This alarm is generated by a Tunnel OAM enabled NE when the OAM protocol
negotiation fails on NEs at both ends of a tunnel.
possible_causes: The OAM function is enabled only on the NE at one end of the tunnel. The OAM enabled end reports the MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL alarm. Figure 4-15 MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL alarm detection (1) Backward tunnel Local end: MPLS Tunnel OAM is enabled. Remote end: MPLS Tunnel OAM is disabled. MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL is reported. Service flow Forward tunnel PSN NOTE Only the NE where the OAM function is enabled will report the MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL alarm. As shown in Figure 4-15, only the local NE reports the MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL alarm.

The tunnel has been interrupted when the OAM function is enabled. Figure 4-16 MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL alarm detection (2) MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL is reported A section of the forward tunnel is interrupted. Backward tunnel Local end Remote end Service flow Forward tunnel PSN OptiX OSN 8800/6800/3800 Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms Issue 01 (2017-03-31) Huawei Proprietary and Confidential Copyright © Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 765 NOTE As shown in Figure 4-16, the MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL alarm is reported by the remote NE when the forward tunnel is interrupted and by the local NE when the reverse tunnel is interrupted.
MPLS_TUNNEL_OAMFAIL.impact: When this alarm occurs, services carried by the faulty tunnel may be interrupted.

MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG.name: MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG
MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG.description:
The MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG alarm indicates that an MEG is unexpected on a tunnel.
This alarm indicates that the MEP receives CCM packets with the correct MEG level but
incorrect MEG ID.
possible_causes: There are multiple tunnels with the same MEG ID between the source and sink NEs. An example is provided as follows: As shown in Figure 4-18, there are two links that are connected to NE2 in the network plan: tunnel 1 between NE1 and NE2, and tunnel 2 between NE3 and NE2. The MEG ID of tunnel 1 is 1 and that of tunnel 2 is 2. However, in actual configuration, outgoing MEG IDs of both tunnel 1 and tunnel 2 are set to 1. NE2 receives a CCM packet that contains incorrect MEG ID from NE3. As a result, NE2 reports the MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG alarm. MEG IDs are inconsistent on NEs at both ends of a tunnel. An example is provided as follows: As shown in Figure 4-19, NE2 is the source end for NE1 and the MEG ID on both NEs is 1 in the network plan. However, the MEG ID of NE1 is set to 1 while that of NE2 is set to 2 in fact. Therefore, NE2 reports the MPLS_PW_UNEXPMEP alarm upon receiving the CCM packet with an incorrect MEG ID from NE1. Physical links are connected incorrectly. Multiple tunnels with the same MEG ID are connected to the same sink NE. As shown in Figure 4-20, a fiber between NE1 and NE2 is connected correctly. The tunnel between NE1 and NE2 has an outgoing label (label 1) and the MEG ID is 1. The tunnel between NE3 and NE4 has an outgoing label (label 1) and the MEG ID is 2. In practice, if NE2 is mistakenly connected to NE3, the outgoing label of a tunnel on NE1 is the same as that of the tunnel from NE3 to NE4, and the incoming label of a tunnel on NE2 is the same as the outgoing label of a tunnel from NE3 to NE4. As a result, NE2 reports the MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG alarm. MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEG.impact: When this alarm is generated, packets on other tunnels are received over this tunnel.

MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP.name: MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP
MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP.description:
The MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP alarm indicates that an MEP is unexpected on a tunnel.
This alarm is reported when the MEP receives CCM packets with the correct MEG level,
correct MEG ID, but unexpected MEP ID.
possible_causes: MEP IDs are inconsistent on NEs at both ends of the tunnel. As shown in Figure 4-21, NE2 is the source end for NE1 and the MEP ID on both NEs is 1. However, the MEP ID of NE1 is set to 1 while that of NE2 is set to 2 in fact. Therefore, NE2 reports the MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP alarm upon receiving the CCM packet with an unexpected MEP ID from NE1. Figure 4-21 MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP alarm detection MEP ID = 1 MEP ID = 2 NE2 reports the MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP alarm. Service flow NE1 NE2 Tunnel PSN OptiX OSN 8800/6800/3800 Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms Issue 01 (2017-03-31) Huawei Proprietary and Confidential Copyright © Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 773
The physical link has an incorrect connection.
MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPMEP.impact:
When this alarm is generated, the services may be interrupted or packets on other tunnels are
received over this tunnel.

MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPPER.name: MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPPER
MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPPER.description:
The MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPPER alarm indicates that the tunnel period is unexpected. This
alarm is reported when the MEP receives CCM packets with the correct MEG level, MEG ID,
and MEP ID, but the period carried in the packets is different from the period for the MEP to
transmit packets.
possible_causes: The tunnel configurations are incorrect and the periods configured at the source and sink NEs are different.
The physical link has an incorrect connection.
MPLS_TUNNEL_UNEXPPER.impact:
When this alarm is generated, the services may be interrupted or packets on other tunnels are
received over this tunnel.

OMS_LOSS_ACCUM_ABN.name: OMS_LOSS_ACCUM_ABN
OMS_LOSS_ACCUM_ABN.description:
Abnormal accumulated span loss. This alarm is generated when the actual span loss is
different from the gain compensation value and the accumulated difference of all spans
exceeds the threshold.
OMS_LOSS_ACCUM_ABN.impact:
If the line loss is excessively large, service signals may be unstable and BER may increase.
Then, an alarm indicating excessively low path optical power may occur and the performance
may be abnormal.

OSNR_LOSS_UNBALANCED.name: OSNR_LOSS_UNBALANCED
OSNR_LOSS_UNBALANCED.description:
Unbalanced OSNR loss flatness alarm. This alarm is generated when the difference between
the OSNR loss of monitored wavelengths and the average loss exceeds the threshold.
OSNR_LOSS_UNBALANCED.impact:
If the single-wavelength OSNR loss is abnormal, service signals may be unstable and the
BER may increase. Then an alarm indicating excessively low or high path optical power may
occur and the performance may be abnormal.

PASSWORD_NEED_CHANGE.name: PASSWORD_NEED_CHANGE
PASSWORD_NEED_CHANGE.description:
The password of a default user must be changed to reduce risks. This alarm is generated if the
password of any default user is not changed in time.

PATCH_BD_EXCLUDE.name: PATCH_BD_EXCLUDE
PATCH_BD_EXCLUDE.description:
Isolation of a patch package board.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
883
PATCH_BD_EXCLUDE.impact: The board is isolated, and patch matching and loading stop.

PATCH_BD_MATCH_FAIL.name: PATCH_BD_MATCH_FAIL
PATCH_BD_MATCH_FAIL.impact:
If the board fails to match the patch package, the patch status may be inconsistent.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
884

PATCH_CHGSCC_NOTMATCH.name: PATCH_CHGSCC_NOTMATCH
PATCH_CHGSCC_NOTMATCH.description: Patch inconsistency after the system control board is replaced.
PATCH_CHGSCC_NOTMATCH.impact:
After the system control board is replaced, if the board patch status is inconsistent with the
patch package status, patch synchronization cannot be automatically performed.

PORT_WLLCFG_REPEATED.name: PORT_WLLCFG_REPEATED
PORT_WLLCFG_REPEATED.description: Repeated wavelength locking configurations are present on an optical port of an OTU board.
PORT_WLLCFG_REPEATED.impact:
Wavelength locking adjustment cannot be performed on the optical port where the alarm is
generated.

PUMP_LINK_ULLAGE_HIGH.name: PUMP_LINK_ULLAGE_HIGH
PUMP_LINK_ULLAGE_HIGH.description:
Pump laser connection insertion loss alarm. The alarm indicates that the insertion loss
between the pump laser and the optical amplifier module exceeds the threshold.
PUMP_LINK_ULLAGE_HIGH.impact:
The connection insertion loss is excessively high, which weakens the amplifying ability of the
optical amplifier board. In this case, the amplifying specifications required by the system
cannot be satisfied, which brings impact on the service quality.

PWAPS_TYPE_MISMATCH.name: PWAPS_TYPE_MISMATCH
PWAPS_TYPE_MISMATCH.description:
The PWAPS_TYPE_MISMATCH alarm indicates that the local NE and the peer NE have
different PW protection types. This alarm is generated when the PW protection type indicated
in the received automatic protection switching (APS) frame is different from that specified on
the local NE.
possible_causes: The protection modes (1+1 or 1:1) are different.
The switching modes (single-ended or dual-ended) are different.
The revertive modes (revertive or non-revertive) are different.
PWAPS_TYPE_MISMATCH.impact:
Service protection may fail.
The following figure shows the major suppression relationship between the alarm and other

RACK_CONFLICT_SCREEN.name: RACK_CONFLICT_SCREEN
RACK_CONFLICT_SCREEN.description:
This alarm is reported after the board isolates the subrack ID conflict caused by incorrect
connections between device cascading ports.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
925
RACK_CONFLICT_SCREEN.impact:
Since the board isolates the subrack ID conflict, the communication is not affected
temporarily but potential communication risks are present. Therefore, the subrack ID conflict
needs to be manually rectified.

RELAY_ALARM_CRITICAL.name: RELAY_ALARM_CRITICAL
RELAY_ALARM_CRITICAL.description: Critical alarm of the alarm input.
RELAY_ALARM_CRITICAL.impact:
For the port of the EFI1 board changes.
For the port of the EFI board changes.
For the port of the AUX board changes.

RELAY_ALARM_MINOR.name: RELAY_ALARM_MINOR
RELAY_ALARM_MINOR.description: Minor alarm of the alarm input.
RELAY_ALARM_MINOR.impact:
For the port of the EFI1 board changes.
For the port of the EFI board changes.
For the port of the AUX board changes.

RMON_ALM_INBADOCTS_OVER.name: RMON_ALM_INBADOCTS_OVER
RMON_ALM_INBADOCTS_OVER.description:
Statistics of receiving bad packets is over the upper threshold. The alarm is generated when
the octet number of bad packets detected by the Ethernet port of the board crosses the upper
threshold.
RMON_ALM_INBADOCTS_OVER.impact: The Ethernet service quality is degraded.

RXCFG_WAVEDATA_MIS.name: RXCFG_WAVEDATA_MIS
RXCFG_WAVEDATA_MIS.description:
The RXCFG_WA VEDATA_MIS alarm indicates that the physical receive wavelength or band
attribute (odd or even) of an optical module is different from the logical receive wavelength or
band attribute set by a user. This alarm is reported when the receive wavelength or band
attribute settings mismatch on a board and an NE.
possible_causes: The configured logical receive wavelength or band is different from the actually supported receive wavelength or band. OptiX OSN 8800/6800/3800 Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms Issue 01 (2017-03-31) Huawei Proprietary and Confidential Copyright © Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. 941
The board is faulty.
RXCFG_WAVEDATA_MIS.impact: When this alarm is generated, services may be interrupted.

SERVICE_CAPACITY_EXCEED_LICENSE.name: SERVICE_CAPACITY_EXCEED_LICENSE
SERVICE_CAPACITY_EXCEED_LICENSE.description:
Service capacity exceeding the license limit. This alarm indicates that the service capacity
configured in a subrack exceeds the license limit.
SERVICE_CAPACITY_EXCEED_LICENSE.impact:
When the SERVICE_CAPACITY_EXCEED_LICENSE alarm is generated, neither the
existing services nor the operation of the system is affected; however, services corresponding
to the alarm cannot be configured for the subrack where the alarm is generated.

SERVICE_TYPE_EXCEED_LICENSE.name: SERVICE_TYPE_EXCEED_LICENSE
SERVICE_TYPE_EXCEED_LICENSE.description:
Service type exceeding the license limit. This alarm indicates that the type of configured
services exceeds the license limit.
SERVICE_TYPE_EXCEED_LICENSE.impact:
When the SERVICE_TYPE_EXCEED_LICENSE alarm is generated, neither the existing
services nor the operation of the system is affected; however, services corresponding to the
alarm cannot be configured for the subrack where the alarm is generated.

SHELF_AREA_POWER_OVER.name: SHELF_AREA_POWER_OVER
SHELF_AREA_POWER_OVER.description:
Total optical power consumption of a subrack section exceeding the threshold. This alarm is
generated when the total power consumption of the boards in a section of the subrack is
higher than or equal to the power consumption threshold for this section.
SHELF_AREA_POWER_OVER.impact:
The total power consumption of the boards in a section of the subrack exceeds the threshold,
making the system in a dangerous state. If the system runs in this state for a long period of
time, the power supply unit of the subrack may work abnormally and a power failure may
occur in the subrack.

SHELF_POWER_UNCONFIG.name: SHELF_POWER_UNCONFIG
SHELF_POWER_UNCONFIG.description:
The power consumption threshold of a subrack is not configured. This alarm is reported if the
power consumption threshold of a subrack is not configured during new deployment or after
the NE database is cleared and the NE is reset.
SHELF_POWER_UNCONFIG.impact:
If the power consumption threshold of a subrack is not configured, the default threshold will
be used by the system. As a result, the power supply unit of the subrack may work abnormally
and a power failure may occur in the subrack in some cases.

SLAVE_WORKING.name: SLAVE_WORKING
SLAVE_WORKING.description:
The SLA VE_WORKING is an alarm indicating the working state of the standby board. If the
standby cross-connect board is selected for the service bus of the service board, and if the
standby clock is selected as the system clock, the SLA VE_WORKING alarm is reported.
possible_causes: The active cross-connect board is not in position.
The active cross-connect board is faulty.
The service board is faulty.
SLAVE_WORKING.impact:
When the SLA VE_WORKING alarm is generated, the system is not affected. This alarm just
indicates that the standby cross-connect board is selected for the service bus of the service
board, and the standby clock is selected as the system clock.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
950

SPAN_LOSS_EXCEED_EOL.name: SPAN_LOSS_EXCEED_EOL
SPAN_LOSS_EXCEED_EOL.description:
Span fiber loss exceeding EOL. This alarm is generated when the actual fiber loss is larger
than the EOL value.
SPAN_LOSS_EXCEED_EOL.impact:
If the line loss is excessively large, service signals may be unstable and BER may increase.
Then an alarm indicating excessively low path optical power may occur and the performance
may be abnormal.

SPAN_LOSS_LOWER_GAIN.name: SPAN_LOSS_LOWER_GAIN
SPAN_LOSS_LOWER_GAIN.description:
Span loss lower than the gain compensation value. This alarm is generated when the actual
span loss is smaller than the power compensation value and the difference between the two
exceeds the specified threshold.
SPAN_LOSS_LOWER_GAIN.impact:
Service signals may be unstable, bit errors may increase, and even abnormal performance may
result.

SPAN_LOSS_UPPER_GAIN.name: SPAN_LOSS_UPPER_GAIN
SPAN_LOSS_UPPER_GAIN.description:
Span loss upper than the gain compensation value. This alarm is generated when the actual
span loss is larger than the power compensation value and the difference between the two
exceeds the specified threshold.
SPAN_LOSS_UPPER_GAIN.impact:
Service signals may be unstable, bit errors may increase, and even abnormal performance may
result.

SSL_CERT_DAMAGED.name: SSL_CERT_DAMAGED
SSL_CERT_DAMAGED.description: User-defined SSL certificate file damaged alarm.
SSL_CERT_DAMAGED.impact:
If this alarm is not immediately cleared, an attempt to log in to an NE in SSL mode will fail
after a system reset.

STORM_CUR_QUENUM_OVER.name: STORM_CUR_QUENUM_OVER
STORM_CUR_QUENUM_OVER.description:
Alarm storm. Some alarms on the system control board may be lost when the alarm queue is
full. This alarm indicates that the alarm module is in the alarm storm state.
STORM_CUR_QUENUM_OVER.impact:
Some alarms may be overwritten when there are excessive alarms. As a result, the alarm
status of the NE is inappropriate.

SUBRACK_ID_MISMATCH.name: SUBRACK_ID_MISMATCH
SUBRACK_ID_MISMATCH.impact:
The DIP switch of the subrack ID mismatches the subrack ID saved by the NE software,
which leads to the abnormal communication between the boards.

SUBRACK_TYPE_MISMATCH.name: SUBRACK_TYPE_MISMATCH
SUBRACK_TYPE_MISMATCH.impact:
The alarm does not affect the existing services and the operation of the system. Services,
however, cannot be configured for the subrack that generates this alarm. If an incorrect logical
slave subrack is deleted, services will be interrupted, and can be restored after a logical slave
subrack and services are configured again. For an incorrect logical master subrack, if another
NE is created, the services traversing the original NE will be interrupted, and can be restored
after a logical master subrack and services are configured again.

SWDL_ACTIVATED_TIMEOUT.name: SWDL_ACTIVATED_TIMEOUT
SWDL_ACTIVATED_TIMEOUT.description:
Activation timeout. This alarm is generated when the activation operation is not committed
within 120s after the activation is complete during software package loading.
SWDL_ACTIVATED_TIMEOUT.impact: This alarm has no impact on services.

SWDL_AUTOMATCH_INH.name: SWDL_AUTOMATCH_INH
SWDL_AUTOMATCH_INH.description:
Automatic match inhibited. This alarm indicates that the automatic matching function is
disabled.
NOTE
After the automatic matching function is enabled, when a board is added to an NE, the system automatically
checks whether the board software matches the NE software. If the board software does not match the NE
software, the system control board upgrades the software of the new board.
SWDL_AUTOMATCH_INH.impact:
The system control board cannot automatically update the software of the board that is newly
inserted. If the software of the new board mismatches the NE software, some functions of the
NE may operate abnormally.

SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH.name: SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH
SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH.description:
Software mismatching alarm after system control board replacement. The system re-checks
whether the software of each board matches the NE software after the NE starts up upon a
power failure or the system control board is replaced or reset (cold). This alarm is generated
when the board software of a board mismatches the NE software.
SWDL_CHGMNG_NOMATCH.impact:
l When this alarm occurs, the automatic matching function for package loading is
disabled.
l The version of the NE software is inconsistent with that of the system control board.
Certain functions of the NE may operate abnormally.

SYSPARA_CFDB_NOSAME.name: SYSPARA_CFDB_NOSAME
SYSPARA_CFDB_NOSAME.description:
Inconsistency between the data in the system parameter area and the CF card. The system
checks the consistency between the data on the system control board and the CF card. If they
are inconsistent, the system does not back up the data but generates this alarm. If they are
consistent, the system backs up the data.
SYSPARA_CFDB_NOSAME.impact:
The data in the system parameter area is inconsistent with that saved in the CF card. The data
cannot be restored from the CF card.

TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADED.name: TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADED
TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADED.description:
The TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADED alarm indicates the degradation of a tunnel protection
group. This alarm is generated when one tunnel of a tunnel APS group becomes abnormal and
the usability of the protection group is impaired. The alarm is cleared if either of the following
conditions is met:
l After the protection tunnel recovers, both the working and protection tunnels are
available.
l Both the working and protection tunnels are unavailable.
possible_causes: One tunnel of a tunnel APS group becomes abnormal.
TUNNEL_APS_DEGRADED.impact:
Availability of the protection group is lowered. Services may be interrupted if the protection
switching occurs.

TUNNEL_APS_OUTAGE.name: TUNNEL_APS_OUTAGE
TUNNEL_APS_OUTAGE.description:
The TUNNEL_APS_OUTAGE alarm indicates that the tunnel APS protection group fails.
When both the working and protection tunnels in an APS protection group fail, the APS
protection group fails and the alarm is reported. The alarm is cleared after either the working
or protection tunnel is restored.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
1023
TUNNEL_APS_OUTAGE.impact:
Availability of the APS protection group is lowered. Services may be interrupted if the
protection switching occurs.

WAVE_ADD_ABN.name: WAVE_ADD_ABN
WAVE_ADD_ABN.impact:
The APE cannot detect wavelength adding.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 4 Clearing Alarms
1033

WAVE_DROP_ABN.name: WAVE_DROP_ABN
WAVE_DROP_ABN.impact: The APE cannot detect wavelength dropping.

WAVEDATA_MIS.name: WAVEDATA_MIS
WAVEDATA_MIS.description:
Mismatch of wavelength or band attributes. This alarm is generated when the configured logic
wavelength or band differs with the actual wavelength or band.
possible_causes: The configured logic wavelength or band differs with the actual wavelength or band.
The board is faulty.

WAVELEN_OVER.name: WAVELEN_OVER
WAVELEN_OVER.description:
Wavelength crossing the threshold. This alarm is generated when the wavelength drift of the
OTU board exceeds the threshold.
WAVELEN_OVER.impact:
The services carried by the wavelength are degraded or interrupted and the services carried by
the adjacent wavelengths may be affected.

WAVELEN_REPEATED.name: WAVELEN_REPEATED
WAVELEN_REPEATED.description:
Repeated wavelengths in the wavelength locking configurations. This alarm is generated
when repeated wavelengths are found in the wavelength locking configurations of the WMU
board.
WAVELEN_REPEATED.impact:
The wavelength locking function of the WMU board is abnormal. As a result, the
wavelengths of the OTU board may be falsely adjusted.

AUPJCHIGH.name: AUPJCHIGH
AUPJCHIGH.description:
Positive justification count of the administrative unit (AU) pointer.
Impact on System
A small number of positive justification events of the AU pointer occur in the data segment,
which does not affect the system. If the pointer justification event occurs frequently, you need
to check the causes and rectify the frequent adjustments so that the system runs stably.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
The root cause of the AU pointer justification is that the clocks of NEs in the SDH network
are asynchronous. The possible causes of the event are as follows:
l The performance of the external clock deteriorates.
l The clocks on two NEs trace each other because optical fibers are connected incorrectly.
l The equipment performance deteriorates due to high temperature.
l The clocks are configured incorrectly. If the extended SSM protocol is enabled but clock
IDs are not set, the loss of the primary clock source causes the network-wide pointer
justification event.
l The clock quality deteriorates because the SSM clock protection is disabled.
l The performance of the line board deteriorates.
l The performance of the clock board deteriorates.
Related Alarms
None.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 6 Handling Performance Events
1304

AUPJCLOW.name: AUPJCLOW
AUPJCLOW.description:
Negative justification count of the administrative unit (AU) pointer
Impact on System
A small number of negative justification events of the AU pointer occur in the data segment,
which does not affect the system. If the pointer justification event occurs frequently, you need
to check the causes and rectify the frequent adjustments so that the system runs stably.

Related Alarms

1305

AUPJCNEW.name: AUPJCNEW
AUPJCNEW.description:
New count of the administrative unit (AU) pointer
Impact on System
A new count of AU pointers is generated, which does not affect the system. If a new count of
AU pointers is generated frequently, you need to check the causes and rectify the frequent
adjustments so that the system runs stably.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
The root cause of generating new data flag (pointer) for the AU pointer justification event is
that the clocks of NEs on the SDH network are asynchronous. As a result, the new AU data
flag (pointer) event is generated. The possible causes are as follows:

1306

BCV.name: BCV
BCV.description:
Pump laser back facet current
It includes:
l BCVMAX: stands for the maximum value during a period of time.
l BCVMIN: stands for the minimum value during a period of time.
l BCVCUR: stands for the current value.
Impact on System
None
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
Back facet current is current O/E converted from part of light reflected from the resonant
cavity of a laser. The back facet current reflects the laser output optical power value. If the
BCVCUR is 0, the laser is faulty. When this occurs, replace the board where this faulty laser
resides.
Related Alarms
None

BDTEMP.name: BDTEMP
BDTEMP.description:
Board temperature. It contains the BDTEMPMAX, BDTEMPMIN, and BDTEMPCUR,
which respectively indicates the maximum value, minimum value, and current value of the
temperature of a board.
Impact on System
Excessively high or low board temperature might cause faults such as degradation of the
board working performance and bit errors.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
When the ambient temperature is abnormal, or when the heat-sinking and ventilation
measures are inappropriate, the BDTEMP event occurs.
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
TEMP_OVER This alarm is reported when the board temperature
exceeds the threshold.

CCV.name: CCV
CCV.description:
Pump laser cooling current
It includes:
l CCVMAX: stands for the maximum value during a period of time.
l CCVMIN: stands for the minimum value during a period of time.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 6 Handling Performance Events
1308
l CCVCUR: stands for the current value.
Impact on System
None
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
An A/D converter is used to sample the voltage corresponding to the cooling current of each
laser, and convert the voltage into cooling current. This value shows the working status of the
cooling circuit in a laser.
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
PUMP_COOL_EXC This alarm is generated when the cooling
current of the laser exceeds the permitted
range.

CFP_LSBIAS.name: CFP_LSBIAS
CFP_LSBIAS.description:
Bias current of the laser on the channel of the CFP module.
It includes:
l CFP_LSBIASMAX: stands for the maximum value during a period of time.
l CFP_LSBIASMIN: stands for the minimum value during a period of time.
l CFP_LSBIASCUR: stands for the current value.
Impact on System
None
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 6 Handling Performance Events
1309
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
The performance value is obtained by hardware check and software conversion.
Related Alarms
None

CFP_LSTMP.name: CFP_LSTMP
CFP_LSTMP.description:
Working temperature of the laser on the channel of the CFP module.
It includes:
l CFP_LSTMPMAX: stands for the maximum value during a period of time.
l CFP_LSTMPMIN: stands for the minimum value during a period of time.
l CFP_LSTMPCUR: stands for the current value.
Impact on System
None
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 6 Handling Performance Events
1311
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
In normal cases, the laser temperature is a stable value obtained by software through
calculating the result output by the temperature detecting circuit in the laser.
Related Alarms
None

CRC4ES.name: CRC4ES
CRC4ES.description:
CRC4 errored seconds
Impact on System
There are bit errors in the services. If the CRC4 errored seconds are generated continuously,
identify the cause and solve the problem in a timely manner to avoid any alarm, therefore
ensuring the signal transmission quality.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
CRC error is detected by checking the received parity bit. An errored second contains more
than one error block.
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
CRC4_CROSSTR CRC4 multi-frame error code exceeds the
threshold. This alarm is generated when the
number of bit errors in the CRC4 multi-
frame exceeds the threshold.

CRC4FEES.name: CRC4FEES
CRC4FEES.description:
CRC4 far end errored second
Impact on System
There are bit errors in the services. If the far-end errored seconds are generated continuously,
identify the cause and solve the problem in a timely manner to avoid any alarm, therefore
ensuring the signal transmission quality. If the number of bit errors exceeds the threshold, the
CRC4_CROSSTR alarm is generated.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
CRC error is detected by checking the received parity bit. An errored second contains more
than one error block. And the far end errored second refers to the errored second detected at
the opposite end.
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
CRC4_CROSSTR CRC4 multi-frame error code counter
exceeds the threshold. This alarm is
generated when the number of bit errors in
the CRC4 multiframe exceeds the threshold.

CRC4FESES.name: CRC4FESES
CRC4FESES.description:
CRC4 far end severely errored second
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 6 Handling Performance Events
1313
Impact on System
There are many bit errors in the services. Identify the cause and solve the problem in a timely
manner to avoid any alarm, and therefore ensuring the signal transmission quality. If the
number of bit errors exceeds the threshold, the CRC4_CROSSTR alarm is generated.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
CRC error is detected by checking the received parity bit. During a severely errored second,
there is at least one defect or 15% of the data blocks are error blocks. And the far end severely
errored second refers to the severely errored second detected at the opposite end.
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
CRC4_CROSSTR CRC4 multi-frame error code count exceeds
the threshold. This alarm is generated when
the number of bit errors in the CRC4
multiframe exceeds the threshold.

CRC4FEUAS.name: CRC4FEUAS
CRC4FEUAS.description:
CRC4 far end unavailable second
Impact on System
There are bit errors in the services. Identify the cause and solve the problem in a timely
manner because the bit errors have affected the signal transmission quality. If the number of
bit errors exceeds the threshold, the CRC4_CROSSTR alarm is generated.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
CRC error is detected by checking the received parity bit. If the severely errored seconds last
for more than 10 seconds, the unavailable second starts from the beginning of the 11th
second, and the former 10 severely errored seconds are counted as unavailable. If the severely
errored second disappears for more than 10 seconds, the available time starts from the
beginning of the 11th second, and the former 10 seconds are counted as available.
Alarms and Performance Events Reference 6 Handling Performance Events
1314
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
CRC4_CROSSTR CRC4 multi-frame bit error count exceeds
the threshold. This alarm is generated when
the number of bit errors in the CRC4
multiframe exceeds the threshold.

DGD.name: DGD

Polarization mode dispersion
It includes:
l DGDMAX: stands for the maximum value.
l DGDMIN: stands for the minimum value.
l DGDCUR: stands for the current value.

Impact on System
A small number of bit errors occur on the higher-order path. If no related alarm is generated,
the system is not affected. You need to, however, identify the causes and resolve the problem
in a timely manner. Otherwise, alarms may be generated, and the signal transmission quality
of the higher-order path deteriorates.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
The HPBBEs are detected by monitoring the B3 byte. The possible causes of the event are as
follows:
l There is interference from the external environment.
l A fault occurs on the switch that interconnects with the SDH equipment.
l The signal cable is faulty.
l The line board malfunctions.
l The cross-connection unit is faulty.
l The clock unit is faulty.

Alarm Name Correlation
B3_SD This alarm is generated when the B3 bit error rate on the alarm path
exceeds the threshold (1×10–6).
B3_EXC This alarm is generated when the B3 bit error rate on the alarm path
exceeds the threshold (1×10-3).

(consecutive severely errored second) is accompanied by the B3_EXC alarm. Consequently,
the services are interrupted. The possible causes of the event are as follows:
l There is interference from the external environment.
l A fault occurs in the switch that interworks with the SDH equipment.
l The signal cable is faulty.
l The line board is faulty.
l The cross-connection unit is faulty.
l The clock unit is faulty.
l The tributary unit is faulty.
Related Alarms
Alarm Name Correlation
B3_SD When the count of B3 bit errors in the alarm path is close to the
threshold (1 x 10-6), the alarm is reported.
B3_EXC When the count of B3 bit errors in the alarm path exceeds the
threshold (1 x 10-3), the alarm is reported.

Impact on System
If bit errors occur in the services on a remote NE, identify the causes and resolve the problem
in a timely manner. Otherwise, alarms may be generated, and the signal transmission quality
deteriorates.
Generation Principle and Possible Causes
HPFEUAS indicates the period of time that the UAT state lasts.
External causes:
l The fiber performance deteriorates or the attenuation is excessive on the remote NE.
l The fiber connector is contaminated or incorrect on the remote NE.
l The remote NE is improperly grounded.
l There is a strong interference source around the remote NE.
l The peer NE runs in an environment with a temperature that exceeds the threshold.
Equipment problems:
l The signals received by the line board on the remote NE are greatly attenuated, the
transmitting circuit on the remote end is faulty, or the receive circuit on the local end is
faulty.
l The synchronization performance of the clock is poor on the remote NE.
l The cross-connection unit and the line board do not match on the remote NE.
l The fan on the remote NE is faulty.
l The board malfunctions or the board performance deteriorates on the remote NE.

Impact on System

seconds, and the bit error rate per second is less than 10-3, the period from the first second is

blocks are detected. The possible causes of the event are as follows:
